description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9 (the op/ census residue's
20-49-row band).  It is the WHOLE of t/op/override.t: 34 blessed fail rows and
16 rows the file never produced.

PERL: a builtin can be overridden two ways, and both are decided at COMPILE
time, when the op is built:
  * `*CORE::GLOBAL::NAME = sub {...}` overrides the keyword NAME for every
    package (`use subs` / `CORE::GLOBAL::` is the documented mechanism);
  * `*main::NAME = sub {...}` overrides it for code compiled after the
    assignment in that package, for the subset of keywords that may be
    overridden (perlsub "Overriding Built-in Functions").

PCL: neither is honoured.  The transpiler emits the builtin's own call form
(`(p-getlogin)`, `(p-time)`, â¦) and nothing consults a user sub of that name.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, probes/p1.pl F6):

    BEGIN { package Foo; *main::getlogin = sub { "kilroy" } }
    printf "getlogin=%s\n", (getlogin() // '(undef)');
    BEGIN { *CORE::GLOBAL::time = sub () { 42 } }
    printf "time=%s\n", time;

    perl: getlogin=kilroy   time=42
    PCL:  getlogin=bernt    time=1789675147

WHAT IT COSTS: t/op/override.t is 36 perl rows and is ABOUT this and nothing
else -- `getlogin`, `time`, `require` (which has special behaviour: the
override is called with the FILENAME perl computed, so `require Foo::Bar`
passes "Foo/Bar.pm"), `readline`/`<>`, `readpipe`/backticks/`qx`, `do`, and
"keywords respect global constant overrides".  34 rows are blessed failures
and the file stops partway (16 rows never produced), so it is the largest
single fact in the t6b band after the filetest one.

WHY IT IS NOT A FILLER: this is a NEW MECHANISM, and the two halves need
different ones.
  * `*CORE::GLOBAL::NAME = sub {...}` is a GLOB ASSIGNMENT, so the compiler
    cannot see it the way it sees `sub NAME {...}` -- `declared_subs` is not
    the seam.  A compile-time answer would need the compiler to treat a glob
    assignment to a CORE::GLOBAL:: slot as a declaration, which is only sound
    when it happens in a BEGIN block (as it does in every real use, and as
    perl requires).
  * a RUNTIME answer -- every builtin's emission checking a table first -- is
    a per-call cost on every builtin in every program, which is the opposite
    of Target A.  A middle road: the compiler emits the ordinary call unless
    the program contains a BEGIN-time glob assignment to `CORE::GLOBAL::` or
    to the builtin's own name, and emits a dispatching form only for the
    keywords that assignment names.  That is one pre-pass over the document
    plus one emission rule, and it is the shape to cost first.

DO NOT RETRY as a runtime-only patch in `p-<builtin>`: an override must also
change how the ARGUMENTS are parsed for `require`/`do`, and a runtime hook
inside `p-require` cannot give the override perl's computed filename without
duplicating the module-name-to-path rule.

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv `op/override.t` (34) +
baselines/row-shortfall.tsv `t/op/override.t` (16).


=== LINKED (s491, Fable, 2026-09-19) ===
The USER's Time::HiRes shim (#1992) needs the IMPORT spelling of this same mechanism, so the two are ONE change: #1992's step 1 IS this task.  The five-spelling probe and perl's rule are written in #1992's "STEP 1 IS TASK #1870" section; `use subs` + a local sub ALREADY works in PCL, so the path exists -- route the imported-glob and CORE::GLOBAL spellings through it.

=== DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
The registry this task needed is `Pl::Environment::builtin_override_target`,
the ONE reading of two records: the package-scoped `overridden_builtins` (now
fed by `use subs` AND by a general module's import list) and a new
`global_builtin_overrides` for `*CORE::GLOBAL::NAME`.  It answers the PACKAGE
whose sub a use site must call, or undef for the builtin;
`builtin_is_overridden` is the boolean half, so the two cannot disagree.

Recorded by `Pl::Parser2::_premerge_builtin_overrides` (the old
`_premerge_use_subs`, widened):
  * `use Module LIST` -- every name in the list that is an overridable (weak)
    keyword.  LANGUAGE pragmas are excluded through the ONE list Parser2 kept
    for the prototype pre-merge, now `$PRAGMA_INCLUDES`; corpus-diff caught
    why (`use feature qw(fc)` imports nothing and `fc` IS a weak keyword, so
    perl-tests/lc.t moved).  A fat comma in the arguments means a KEY => VALUE
    configuration, not names.
  * a glob assignment `*PKG::NAME = <a sub>` INSIDE A BEGIN BLOCK, with perl's
    two conditions probed on 5.40.3: it must be compile time (a run-time
    assignment does NOT displace -- probe row 4) and the CV must come from
    another package (`package P; BEGIN { *P::getppid = ... }` keeps the
    builtin -- row 2, perl's IMPORTED_CV rule).  `CORE::GLOBAL` is exempt from
    the second and displaces for every package.

Emission: a package-scoped override keeps the existing force_user path; a
CORE::GLOBAL one is emitted QUALIFIED (`cl_name("CORE::GLOBAL::$name", 1, 1)`),
in the generic funcall site and in both readpipe sites.

MEASURED: t/op/override.t 3 ok / 17 not-ok -> 9/13, shortfall 16 -> 14; six
rows left baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv by EDIT, verified by a re-run
(0 NEW / 0 FIXED).  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files.  Guard
Pl/t/builtin-override-01.t, 12 rows, six of them the cases a careless fix
breaks (a sub merely DEFINED, a run-time assignment, CORE::, another package),
inverse-verified on a 5ce155cb extraction where 6 fail.

WHAT IS LEFT, filed: #2053 (the `BEGIN { Pkg->import }` spelling, whose names
are not in the source) and #2054 (the CORE::GLOBAL require/do/readline
emission sites -- 28 of the file's remaining rows).


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 1 (0684b77e).  The import and CORE::GLOBAL override
spellings go through the ONE registry `use subs` already fed;
Environment::builtin_override_target answers the PACKAGE whose sub to call and
builtin_is_overridden is its boolean half.  t/op/override.t 3/17 -> 9/13, its
shortfall 16 -> 14, six blessed companion rows removed BY EDIT (3aa37608).
Guard Pl/t/builtin-override-01.t, 12 rows, six of them the cases a careless
fix breaks.  Normative statement: docs/ir-spec.md 7.1a.
LEFT, filed: #2053 (the `BEGIN { Pkg->import }` spelling) and #2054 (the
CORE::GLOBAL require/do/readline emission sites, 28 of the remaining rows).
subject: op/override.t is ONE fact and the whole file: builtin OVERRIDE via *CORE::GLOBAL::NAME or *main::NAME is not honoured -- PCL emits the builtin's own call form (34 blessed rows + 16 never produced)
